Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the manual's own text (Chapter 4, 'What are the Tests Like?', Knowledge test): 'The knowledge test is online and has 20 questions. Each question has four answers to choose from, of which only one is correct. You must answer at least 16 questions correctly to pass the test. If you fail the test, you must wait at least one day before taking another one.' That is 20 questions, need 16 correct (80 percent) to pass, not explicitly stated as timed anywhere in the manual (no time limit is mentioned for the knowledge test, unlike some other states) -- so the real, confirmed mechanics are 20 questions / 80 percent passing threshold / no stated time limit, taken online via mydmv.vermont.gov (the manual states the permit test is no longer given in DMV offices). Vision standard is 20/40. Content-depth rationale: Vermont's manual is a genuinely substantial, 73-page, 12-chapter primary source rich with specific, individually-citable numbers -- statutory citations (7 V.S.A. Section 656, 23 V.S.A. Section 202, 23 V.S.A. Section 1258), exact fee schedules, GDL hour/age/recall requirements, a full point-value table, exact dollar insurance minimums (25,000/50,000/10,000), exact parking-distance and following-distance rules, and detailed sharing-the-road guidance for pedestrians, school buses, bicycles, motorcycles, trucks, and moose/deer. 237 distinct questions were written across 16 topic buckets, every one grounded in and cited to specific manual text (quoted or closely paraphrased in source_note); some thinner administrative chapters (state holidays, office addresses, disability-plate paperwork specifics) were deliberately left mostly untested as low-value trivia rather than padded into filler questions, which is why the total lands at 237 rather than a round 250-300 -- no invented facts, no restated common-knowledge driving trivia outside the manual, and no padding were used to inflate the count.
